chapter_title: Concerning the Alms, that [ ... ] life in the Church.
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by institutional/pastoral exposition about alms, the holy church, and catechumens (¶¶2–6, 11), wrapped in a hagiographic opening (¶1). The oldest teaching substrate appears as a self-contained cosmological mechanism of ascent and rest: the Living Soul in mixture can exit only through the Sun and Moon, and these light-givers rest finally in the Land of Light (¶¶7–10).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic narrative frame (“Once again… The enlightener… He says to his disciples”) typical of Kephalaia compilation apparatus.

Maps alms to contemporary religious landscape (“every sect… their catechumens… holy church… commandments of alms”) and polemic; cosmos→institution pointing, consistent with editorial/institutional layer.
Defines the holy church in social categories (“brothers and sisters”) and treats alms redemption via the church—an institutional mechanism rather than cosmic architecture.
Institutional dependence chain (church ↔ catechumens) expressed as present-world logistics (“in this entire world… through the catechumens”), characteristic of later church operational teaching.

Begins explicitly with catechumen institution (“assembly of catechumens”) and uses an agricultural analogy to motivate their role; the correspondence is deployed to point at a community structure, not to expound cosmic degrees.
Explicit editorial application of the tree/earth analogy to “the [holy] church” and catechumens; institutional vocabulary dominates and completes the pastoral graft.

paragraphs.core_text: Likewise this [liv]ing Sou[l] that today is set in mixture; for it wishes to [as]cend and go to the house of its people, but it kn[ow[s a]nd understands that it has no open door in all the powers of heaven and earth. For they are its oppression that [ ... ] it everywhere. Indeed, it has no open door except the sun and the moon themselves, the light-givers of the heavens [ ... / ... ] they become the place of rest for it. And they become a door that opens for it [in] the coming forth, and (the soul) comes out through them to the country of the household of i[ts] people.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mechanics (mixture → ascent; “open door”; “powers of heaven and earth”; Sun/Moon as functional gateways/rest-stations) stays fully within the cosmic system. The single anchoring word “today” does not redirect to institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, further in, also the light-givers of the heavens have no place of rest amongst all the powers of heaven; except for the lan[d] of light, that has indeed been theirs for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmic-domain mapping: light-givers’ rest-station is the Land of Light; no institutional or audience-address elements.

paragraphs.core_text: So, thus the living soul is purified of all afflictions; and they provide a rest for it, and open a door that opens to the house [of] its people.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same ascent/rest mechanism (purification via cosmic “door” and “rest”), still cosmos→cosmos with no contemporary referents.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, it is the case that the land of lig[ht] will become the final receiver for the light-givers of [the] heavens, and they will rest themselves therein and rule in it [for] ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-closure statement: final receiver/resting place and eternal rule of the light-givers in the Land of Light—structural cosmology typical of the older teaching layer.

Returns to institutional chain (holy church ↔ alms of catechumens) with a concluding nod to the Land of Light; the cosmos is used to validate church practice, indicating late application rather than substrate exposition.
